fases.texto_objetivo: Neil adjusts the sextant under the stars

ficha_info.texto: Commander of the Apollo 11 lunar module, he was the first human to set foot on the Moon on ==July 20, 1969==. His use of the ==space sextant== demonstrated the precision of navigation without a terrestrial reference.

frases: With the ==space sextant== I aligned the ship using the ==Southern Cross== constellation, correcting our trajectory.
Every star is a reference; without land, the sky is our map.

opciones.etiqueta: How did you calibrate the sextant in microgravity?
opciones.respuesta: I adjusted the mirror's angle and verified the position of the known star, compensating for the lack of gravity.
We could correct the trajectory to within ==±5 km==, enough for the rendezvous with the Moon.

frases: I felt the thrill of precision, as if space itself were applauding.
As we approached, the ==Columbia== and ==Eagle== modules made a perfect mechanical docking in the vacuum.
The process required millimeter alignment; any error would have been catastrophic.

opciones.respuesta: We used radar sensors and guidance systems that adjusted the engines in real time.

opciones.etiqueta: How long did the docking take?
opciones.respuesta: About ==12 minutes==, enough for the systems to stabilize the ship.

frases: Seeing the modules embrace was a testament to human engineering.

acciones.descripcion: Neil reviews the angles measured by the sextant to adjust the orbital trajectory.

ficha_info.titulo: Buzz Aldrin — Pilot of the Eagle module
ficha_info.texto: Second man to walk on the Moon, he took part in the mechanical docking between the ==Columbia== and ==Eagle== modules in the ==vacuum== of space, demonstrating the orbital accuracy required for the mission.

frases: From the Eagle module, I watched Columbia approach, each maneuver a dance in the vacuum.
The precision of the docking reminded me of the simulation training on Earth.

opciones.respuesta: We trained with zero-gravity simulators and models of the ship on NASA computers.
Yes, the responsibility of joining the modules was enormous, but trust in the team was greater.

frases: When the coupling was complete, I felt a wave of pride, as if we had joined two worlds.

acciones.descripcion: Buzz inspects the modules' couplings to ensure the mechanical docking in the vacuum.

ficha_info.titulo: Michael Collins — Pilot of the Columbia command module
ficha_info.texto: He orbited the Moon while his companions descended, observed the ==waning Earth== and documented the journey photographically toward the ==Mare Tranquillitatis==, providing critical navigation data.

frases: From Columbia, I watched the docking, ready to intervene if something failed.
My post required me to keep the ship stable while the others worked.

opciones.respuesta: The attitude and propulsion systems, keeping orientation with the thrusters.
Critical; any deviation would have jeopardized the entire mission.

frases: The silence of space was profound, but trust in the crew filled the cabin.
As the ship headed toward the ==Mare Tranquillitatis==, Earth shrank, a blue ball slowly disappearing.
The view reminded me of the fragility of our planet.

opciones.respuesta: I captured images of the lunar surface and of the receding Earth, using the module's high-resolution camera.

opciones.etiqueta: How did that affect your perspective?
opciones.respuesta: It made me value peace and international cooperation, for we all share that little blue dot.

frases: That moment was etched in my memory, as a testament to human exploration.

acciones.descripcion: Michael captures images of ==Earth== from orbit, documenting its appearance and position.

interaccion.descripcion: The ==space sextant== is a navigation instrument that measures the angle between a celestial body and the horizon, allowing the observer's position to be calculated. In the Apollo mission, it was used to correct the orbital trajectory by referencing the ==stars==.
The ==Columbia Command Module== houses the control cabin and the crew during the orbital phase. It has a mass of ==30,000 kg== and contains the navigation, communication and life-support systems.
The ==Eagle Lunar Module== is designed for the Moon landing and the return to orbit. Its dry mass is ==15,000 kg== and it has descent engines that use ==hydrazine== as fuel.

interaccion.texto: S-band parabolic antenna, essential for data communications in orbit.
Exterior navigation camera, captures images of stars and the distant Earth.

zonas_narrativas.texto: Upon entering the scene, the player sees the ==cosmic void== and the shrunken ==Earth==, grasping the scale of the journey.
